newsitem.title: AFGHANISTAN: Taleban say enemy seizes key town north of Kabul.
newsitem.headline: Taleban say enemy seizes key town north of Kabul.

text.p: The Islamic Taleban militia said on Saturday it had lost the key Afghan town of Jabal-os-Siraj to opposition commander Ahmad Shah Masood, cutting off a big Taleban force in the north from its base in the capital Kabul.
Taleban Information Minister Amir Khan Mutaqi told reporters in the northern town of Pul-i-Khumri that Masood's forces were holding Jabal-os-Siraj, about 70 km (56 miles) north of Kabul.

Masood's ethnic Tajik guerrillas burst out of their Panjsher Valley stronghold on Friday to capture the town of Golbahar at the valley's mouth and nearby Jabal-os-Siraj, at the foot of the Salang Pass which runs through the Hindu Kush mountain range and is a crucial gateway between north and south.

A 3,000-strong Taleban force, which crossed the Salang earlier this week to try to link up with Taleban fighters then in the northern capital of Mazar-i-Sharif, is now effectively cut off from its supply lines south of Jabal-os-Siraj.

Mutaqi said fighting was still going on around the town and the Pakistan-based Afghan Islamic Press reported that Taleban warplanes had bombed Masood's positions in the Panjsher Valley from the Soviet-built Bagram airbase north of Kabul.
It said Taleban planes had also launched 60 bombing sorties against Mazar-i-Sharif, where local Uzbek and Shi'ite Moslem forces defeated about 3,000 Taleban fighters earlier in the week.
